name: Ikejiri-Ohashi
tagline: Shibuya in 4 minutes and Shinjuku in 14 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000.
summary: The station is in Meguro City, where Tokyu run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 27 minutes to Otemachi, 14 minutes to Shinjuku, 4 minutes to Shibuya and 30 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. The station stands 17 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 20.0 m. The land around the station rises and falls sharply.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 17 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 13.4 m to 33.4 m, a difference of 20.0 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 3 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 3 clinics and 9 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 古畑クリニック, about 1 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 東邦大学医療センター 大橋病院, about 4 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line.
congestion: Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line runs at 138% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch of the line is 池尻大橋→渋谷, which includes this station. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥110,000 to ¥120,000 and 1K ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. 1LDK ¥210,000 to ¥220,000 and 2LDK ¥300,000 to ¥310,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. What holds the figure down: only one line, the {line}, serving the station and a climb from the station to much of the housing. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Komaba-Todaimae is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection and quiet, but Ikejiri-Ohashi is ahead on how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Ikejiri-Ohashi. Komaba-Todaimae has the Keio Inokashira Line, a different set from Ikejiri-Ohashi. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. A one-room flat costs about ¥8,000 more at Komaba-Todaimae. On quiet, Komaba-Todaimae comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Ikejiri-Ohashi, but Shinsen is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection and the number of medical facilities.
neighbours.note: About 1 km from Ikejiri-Ohashi in a straight line. Shinsen has the Keio Inokashira Line, a different set from Ikejiri-Ohashi. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. A one-room flat costs about ¥42,000 more at Shinsen. On the number of places to eat out, Shinsen comes out ahead.

noiseSources: The 首都高速3号渋谷線 viaduct runs right beside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
玉川通り (3 lanes each way) runs right beside the station. Traffic on it never stops, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station rises and falls sharply, and living above or below the slope changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 5 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyu Den-en-toshi Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are lightly loaded in the morning.
